d.why: A bar worker in Japan who only asks Logan whether he is American and whether he drinks to forget, in one short cut scene that changes nothing, and 'Japanese Bartender' is a job description, not a name.
Scott's mother has at most a line ('He won't listen to us') before Alex takes Scott to the school, one short scene that changes nothing.
Erik's wife in Poland, who knows his secret and talks with him at home, and whose death with Nina at the hands of the police turns him back into Magneto and starts the plot of Apocalypse.
A young mutant who digs through rubble, finds an X-Men badge and is killed by Sentinels in the future-war opening, with no lines, and 'Mutant Scavenger' is a description, not a name.
Ink is one of the captive mutant soldiers Mystique frees in Saigon and later just watches the news; he has no part of his own in the story.
The spiky-headed mutant soldier only stands among the captives Mystique frees in Saigon, with no lines and no part in the plot.

Peter's mother, who speaks in both Days of Future Past (calling him down to the 'cops') and Apocalypse (checking on him when he is about to go after his father Magneto), family with scenes that matter to a lead across two films.
Peter's little sister has one short exchange with Logan about being a princess and watches TV with Peter; that changes nothing, and her credit is a description, not a name.
The President in Days of Future Past, who hears Trask out, approves the Sentinel program and unveils it at the White House, and is held hostage by Magneto; a leader whose orders drive events.
The Secretary of State only speaks in the crisis meeting that sends the fleet, and 'Secretary of State' is a job title, not a name (the owner's rule).
Charles's mother never really appears: the woman in the kitchen is Raven in disguise, so the scene belongs to Raven's file.
The U.S. Navy captain only relays orders during the Cuba blockade, and 'U.S. Navy Captain' is a job description, not a name.
The Soviet captain gives a few orders aboard the missile ship, but 'Russian Navy Captain' is a job description, not a name.
A background Xavier student who laughs at Colossus's drawing in X2 and sits in class in The Last Stand, with no lines and no part in the plot.
The brain-dead patient on Muir Island does nothing himself; his one line, 'Hello, Moira', is Charles speaking after moving into his body, so it belongs to fox-charles-xavier.
Siryn is a Xavier student who screams during Stryker's raid in X2 and stands at Xavier's funeral in The Last Stand, but she has no lines.
Phat is a mutant at the church meeting who fights for the Brotherhood at Alcatraz, with no lines and no part of his own.
Glob Herman is a wax-skinned Brotherhood recruit hit by a cure dart at Alcatraz, with no lines and no part of his own.

Quill (credited as Kid Omega) is an Omega who taunts Pyro at Magneto's rally, guards Jean's house, kills Dr. Rao and throws Worthington off the lab roof ('Do we look like we need your help?'), a henchman with a job in the plot.
Ash is a Brotherhood mutant who burns a soldier during the Alcatraz battle, with no lines and no part of his own.
The President in The Last Stand speaks with Hank and Trask about Magneto and the cure, but he is credited only as 'President', a job title, not a name.
Angel's father, head of Worthington Labs, who makes and announces the mutant cure that drives The Last Stand, tries to cure his own son and is saved by him at Alcatraz.
The White House tour guide only reads Lincoln's words to tourists in the opening before Nightcrawler's attack, one short scene that changes nothing.
One of the Secret Service agents guarding President McKenna during Nightcrawler's attack, with no part of his own in one short scene.
One of the Secret Service agents guarding President McKenna during Nightcrawler's attack, with no part of his own in one short scene.
Mr. Shaw is a TV pundit seen debating Hank McCoy in one background clip that changes nothing.

Bobby's mother, who hears him come out as a mutant in the Boston scene ('Have you tried not being a mutant?') and is held hostage in the police standoff that follows, family with a scene that matters to Iceman.
Bobby's father, who confronts Logan ('Who the hell are you?') and hears Bobby come out as a mutant in the Boston scene before the police standoff, family with a scene that matters to Iceman.
